program: nil [ cons ] fold nil 0 cons [ over uncons swap drop add cons ] fold 0 [ [ lt? ] [ swap ] [ ] ifte drop ] fold
notes: Reformulated the clamped running balance as the largest suffix total: reverse the list, run a prefix-sum fold over the reversal, then a max fold seeded at 0. The closed states are 'the list backwards', 'every suffix total (with 0)', and 'the best of them'.

program: over [ over swap [ eq? ] swap cons filter cat ] fold 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold swap 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold eq? [ ] [ drop 1 ] [ drop 0 ] ifte
notes: Instead of a nested filter over a consed-in list, fold over ys appending to xs every element of the accumulator that the current y matches, so the list grows exactly when something is shared. The closed states are 'xs plus whatever it matched', 'how long that grew to', 'how long xs was', and the flag.

program: nil quote [ over uncons swap drop swap quote cat cons ] fold nil [ cons ] fold uncons drop [ [ lt? ] [ swap ] [ ] ifte drop ] quote [ uncons ] swap cat [ fold ] cat map
notes: Fissioned into 'every prefix' (8-atom body) and 'the max of each prefix', and the max quotation is written separately and bound in so no write run exceeds 12. Blocked by rule 2 only: a max-combine needs ifte with two branch quotations, which is 8 atoms on its own, so any body that wraps it in uncons/fold is at least 10 -- and the single-fold scan (read the head of the accumulator, combine, cons) costs 12. No arrangement I found puts a running maximum inside 8 atoms.

program: over [ drop false ] map cat [ swap uncons [ swap ] dip eq? quote cat ] fold [ true eq? ] filter 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold
notes: Pad ys with one false per element of xs so it never runs out and the padding can never equal an int, then walk xs consuming a head of the accumulator and appending the eq? bool to its tail, so the accumulator ends as the list of verdicts. Closed states: 'the padding', 'ys padded', 'one verdict per position', 'just the matches', 'how many'.

program: dup dup [ over swap [ eq? ] swap cons filter cons ] fold nil [ cons ] fold [ drop uncons drop ] fold dup [ 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold ] map 0 [ [ lt? ] [ swap ] [ ] ifte drop ] fold [ 0 [ drop 1 add ] fold ] swap quote cat [ eq? ] cat filter uncons swap drop uncons swap drop
notes: Each value's occurrence list is prepended to an accumulator that still carries the original values; lists never equal ints so later counts are unaffected. Reverse and drop one head per input to recover just the occurrence lists, which carry both the value (head) and the count (length). Closed states: 'occurrence lists over the values', 'them in order', 'the counts', 'the best count', 'the lists that hit it', and its first value.
